hints.title: Getting the voltage sensor
hints.content: Use `VoltageSensor voltageSensor = hardwareMap.voltageSensor.iterator().next();` to get the first (and usually only) voltage sensor. Then read it with `voltageSensor.getVoltage()`.

hints.title: The normalization formula
hints.content: Scale your desired power by the ratio of nominal to actual voltage: `double scale = 12.0 / voltage;` then `double normalizedPower = 0.7 * scale;`. At 10.5V, scale is 12.0/10.5 ≈ 1.143, so the result is ≈ 0.8.

hints.title: Don't forget to clamp
hints.content: The scaled value can exceed 1.0, which is invalid for setPower(). Clamp it: `normalizedPower = Math.max(-1.0, Math.min(1.0, normalizedPower));`
